tossups.text: In this nation, after an assassination attempt upon a former defense minister, Proclamation No. 1081 imposed martial law, while habeas corpus had been suspended after the earlier Plaza Miranda bombing. Before one battle was fought here, the line "You may fire when ready, Gridley" was said. This country's first post-independence president was Manual Roxas. Cardinal Jaime Sin led the People Power Revolution here, which ultimately placed in power the widow of a politician assassinated in 1983 upon his arrival at the capital's airport. The wife of another of this country's leaders owned over 2700 pairs of shoes. The United States fought a guerrilla war here against Emilio Aguinaldo. For 10 points, name this Pacific nation led by Ferdinand Marcos and Corazon Aquino.

Catharine Greene, wife of Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene, funded the invention of a machine that processed this good. Despite the fact that this good is not edible, the British lamented a "famine" of it caused by a Union Navy blockade. Boll weevils ruin harvests of this good. Eli Whitney designed a "gin" to separate the seeds and fibers of, for 10 points, what textile cash crop that was overwhelmingly grown by slaves in the American South?

A picture frame depicting two people, one in red and another in blue, hangs in the top left of this painting, next to a clock which reads seven o'clock. Spoons hang in the top right of this painting, and a tea kettle sits in this painting's bottom right corner. A hanging oil lamp provides the only source of light in this painting, in which a woman in a white bonnet pours out four cups of tea. The two figures on the left use forks to eat the main dish. For 10 points, name this painting that depicts five peasants around a table having a meal, a work by Vincent van Gogh.

In the story of the Rasa-lila, this instrument provides the music that the gopis of Vrindavana dance to for 4.32 billion years. According to some Chinese legends, one type of this instrument was invented by the Yellow Emperor, though historically it was probably imported during the Han Dynasty. A hunchbacked trickster deity that plays one of these instruments delivers unborn babies to young girls in myths from the American southwest. Krishna is often portrayed in the Tribhanga posture with one of these musical instruments. The Hopi god Kokopelli is commonly depicted playing one of these instruments, which represents his giant penis. For 10 points, name this class of musical instrument invented and played by the Greek god Pan.

This city's Dynamo Stadium hosted a 1996 music festival that was lauded as a key event in its country's cultural freedom. Russky Island is separated from this city by the so-called "Eastern Bosporus," referencing similarity to Constantinople that inspired the name of Golden Horn Bay. It lies between the Ussuri and Amursky Gulfs, and was closed to foreigners for decades due to its housing a naval force that had earlier lost the Battle of Tsushima. Sergei Witte oversaw a major project connecting the capital to this city, the Trans-Siberian Railroad. For 10 points, identify this city lying across the Sea of Japan from Honshu, the largest Pacific port owned by Russia.

Along with the Mediterranean and the Nile, this river made up one of the three arms of the T in the medieval T and O map design. The Maeotian [mee-"OCEAN"] Swamp surrounded the mouth of this river, which was called the Tanais [tah-NAY-iss] by the ancient Greeks. The most populous city along this river is home to a sculpture depicting the characters Grigori and Aksinia in a boat. A reservoir formed on this river submerged the white-bricked fortress of Sarkel, which was used as a base by the Khazars. The naval base of Taganrog is located a few miles west of the mouth of this river. Rostov is the most populous city on this river, which a canal connects to the much longer Volga River.For 10 points, name this river that "quietly flows" in a novel about Cossacks by Mikhail Sholokhov.

This economist collaborated with William James Adams in a 1976 paper arguing against allowing monopolies in bundled commodities. This economist has the alphabetically later surname in a 2004 paper arguing that Robert Lucas's critique of Keynesian ("CANE-zee-in") stabilization policy is inaccurate because workers would be worse off unemployed in a recession than during a boom. In one position, this economist oversaw a process called "unwinding the balance sheet," which was the sell-off of assets acquired during a period of quantitative easing. This economist co-authored many of her famous papers with her husband, George Akerlof, before Barack Obama appointed her to her most famous role. For 10 points, name this Federal Reserve Chair from 2014 to 2018.

Early American imports of this commodity were produced from the guayule plant. The production of this commodity was overseen by an army that severed the hands of people who failed to meet quotas; that army, which was employed in the Congo Free State by Leopold II of Belgium, was called the Force Publique. It is obtained from Haeva brasiliensis, and it was used by pre-Colombian civilizations to produce a spheroid for a ritual ball game. For 10 points, name this commodity whose global demand soared after Charles Goodyear invented vulcanization.

this structure is essential for skeletal muscle structure. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this sarcomere-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The sarcomere is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in skeletal muscle structure.

tossups.text: One equation describing a form of this phenomenon sets the potential proportional to the negative exponential of radius divided by radius; that equation for the Yukawa potential describes the residual form of this phenomenon. Confinement of a certain quantity prevents the free "emission" of this phenomenon, and instead leads to the production of jets of massive particles. This phenomenon is described by quantum chromodynamics, since this interaction's carrier particle possesses a color charge; that carrier particle is the gluon. The force that binds quarks together into nucleons and protons and neutrons together into atomic nuclei is--for 10 points--what fundamental force with a strength approximately 137 times that of electromagnetism?

This thinker blamed social issues on not calling things by their proper names, a problem he resolved with his "rectification of names." This mentor of Mencius advocated for archery and calligraphy in his "Six Arts," which are essential to becoming a perfect gentleman. This thinker developed five kinds of relationships, which are subject to filial piety. For 10 points, name this Ancient Chinese philosopher, whose thoughts are collected in the Analects.

An object that this character goes to great lengths to acquire is immediately stolen by a snake. This character is mistaken for a criminal by the alewife Siduri; earlier, this son of Ninsun encounters two scorpion monsters at Mount Mashu. One of the many beings killed by this character is Gugalanna, an enormous bull sent after this character after he spurns the goddess Ishtar. This character meets a survivor of a great flood named Utnapishtim and travels to the Cedar Forest to kill the giant Humbaba. Enkidu is-for 10 points-the wild companion of which character, the protagonist of a namesake Sumerian epic?

One person with this surname lost a gubernatorial election to the then-incumbent Lawton Chiles, and he declined the position of NFL Commissioner while still Governor. Another person with this surname was mockingly attributed the quote "not gonna do it, wouldn't be prudent," and said on a campaign that there would be "no more taxes". That President won an election alongside Dan Quayle. His elder son also served as President, defeating Al Gore in 2000 and John Kerry in 2004. For ten points, give the surname of former Florida governor Jeb and former presidents George H.W. and George W.

One short story by this man centers on a crow named Schwartz who later identifies himself as the titular avian. One collection by this author includes the stories "A Pimp's Revenge" and "Glass Blower of Venice" both of which focus on the recurring protagonist Arthur Fidelman. This author's most famous work concerns a player who uses the bat "Wonderboy" as he plays for the fictional baseball team the New York Knights. That player's name is Roy Hobbs. For ten points, name this author of The Natural.

Like Sumatra, it was once known as Taprobane thanks to Alexander the Great's general Onesicritus, and classical geographers long debated whether it stretched nearly to the coast of Africa. Fronted on the west by the Gulf of Mannar, this island was formerly connected to the Asian mainland by a series of limestone shoals known as Adam's Bridge. For 10 points, name this teardrop-shaped island on whose eastern side lies the Bay of Bengal and which is separated from India by the Palk Strait, formerly known as Ceylon.

This man won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology for using vivisection and fistulas to study the digestive system. The concept of "reflex at a distance" was expanded on by this man, with a test in which a buzzer being sounded at the same time as an assistant provided food; both the assistant and the buzzer sound triggered the salivation response. For 10 points, name this Russian scientist who studied classical conditioning by feeding dogs.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for sympathetic vs parasympathetic. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cranial nerve-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cranial nerve is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in sympathetic vs parasympathetic.

tossups.text: In a recent season of this show, a man named Dennis decided his heart wasn't really in "the game" and decided to open a boxing gym, while Bunny Colvin lost a job offer from a university and his major's pension after his social experiment became public knowledge. In that season, Brother Mouzone teamed up with the man who had previously shot him to track down and murder the man who had orchestrated Mouzone's shooting. The second season of this show featured the shadowy "Greek," the idiotic Ziggy, and a bunch of prostitutes who suffocated in a freight container, while the first season introduced Stringer Bell and Avon Barksdale. For 10 points, name this show which recently began its fourth season on HBO, a crime drama set in .

One class of proteins involved in this process is characterized by LOV domains bound to flavin mononucleotides. Another group of proteins in this process binds to an FAD cofactor and shows high levels of homology with photolyases. The acid growth hypothesis theorizes that substances, such as indoleacetic acid, initiate this process. PIN proteins are responsible for transport of a chemical central to this process. The Cholodny-Went hypothesis proposed that this process occurs due to a redistribution of auxins, resulting in the elongation of cells on one side of a plant's stem. For 10 points, name this term that describes a plant's tendency to grow towards a source of light.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on descriptive answers like “bending towards light” with “What term describes that process?”

tossups.text: In human anatomy, this structure is essential for cardiac cycle. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this systole-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The systole is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in cardiac cycle.

parts.text: Name this conflict which began after a speech at the Council of Clermont and was preceded by a campaign led by Peter the Hermit that was crushed at the Battle of Civetot.
This city was captured by the Crusaders at the Battle of Ascalon. Torquato Tasso wrote an epic poem about this city "Delivered."
This leader was the first ruler of the Kingdom of Jerusalem until his death in 1100. He came into conflict with Tancred during the march on the city following the siege of Antioch.

bonuses.leadin: Part of this conflict saw massacres of Jews in Worms and Mainz by forces led by Count Emicho. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this former republic whose capital city from 1839 to 1845 was named after the empresario Stephen F. Austin.
This Mexican general and president lost the battle of San Jacinto. He took control of Mexico from Anastasio Bustamante in 1832.
acceptableAnswers: Antonio de Padua María Severino López de Santa Anna y Pérez de Lebrón

parts.text: This battle of the Texas Revolution resulted in the deaths of James Bowie and Davy Crockett. The site of this battle was a Spanish mission in San Antonio founded by Fray Antonio de Olivares.

bonuses.leadin: In 1845 this country was annexed by the United States. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this ruler who overthrew the Median Empire and established the Achaemenid Persian Empire in the sixth century BCE.
After overthrowing the Median Empire, Cyrus the Great defeated this empire's king Croesus at the Battle of Thymbra. This empire was the first to use coins and was located on Asia Minor.
Darius the Great divided the Persian Empire into twenty provinces, each governed by one of these people, who were appointed by the king and held their office indefinitely.

bonuses.leadin: He was preceded by Cambyses I and succeeded by Cambyses II.. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The many names for this figure include Julunggul and Kalseru, and most tribes consider it to be the guardian of water. Most stories also depict it creating billabongs and mountain ridges as it slithered across the land.

This devilish creature, sometimes conflated with the Rainbow Serpent, lives in water holes and swamps and emerges at night to kill evildoers and devour animals. They're also said to produce loud, booming barks or cries.

This four-foot tall vampire-like creature lives in fig trees and eats the bodies of its victims after sucking their blood. Later, after a nap, it regurgitates them, slightly shorter but otherwise unharmed.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these features of Australian Aboriginal mythology, FTPE.

parts.text: Name this most populous city in Canada, the capital of the province of Ontario.

This structure in Toronto was the tallest tower in the world until being surpassed by the Burj Khalifa in 2007. One can do the EdgeWalk around the roof of the main pod of this tower, while being held by a harness.
Toronto is part of one of these groups named after the Great Lakes. These entities are agglomerations of cities or metropolitan areas that have sprawled enough to become connected.

bonuses.leadin: This city's metropolitan area, which includes Mississauga and Brampton, is connected by the historic Dundas Street. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this research base, the U.S.'s largest in Antarctica. It lies on Ross Island, just west of a namesake set of Martian-like arid valleys. It's of sufficient importance that it came up three times in Geography Monstrosity IX ["nine"].

Most of McMurdo's residents - which can number more than 1,000 during the summer - are not scientists, but rather support staff. Until it sold its contract for $5 billion in 2016, this military and aerospace technology company supplied those laborers.

In 2009, Germany's Alfred Wegener [VAY-guh-nur] Institute erected an Antarctic base atop a set of 16 hydraulic pillars used to control snow accumulation. Name that innovative base, which abuts the Weddell Sea.

bonuses.leadin: It boasts three bars: the Coffee House, Gallagher's, and Southern Exposure. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The diagnostic criteria for this personality disorder includes "a grandiose sense of self-importance". In diagnosis, it must be distinguished from other Cluster B disorders like BPD or anti-social personality disorder.
This is the most popular type of therapy for personality disorders. Created by Marsha Linehan, it takes its name from the philosophical process of discourse between opposing individuals.
One Cluster C personality disorder shares its name with this better-known disorder. This disorder is characterised by recurring upsetting and intrusive thoughts and subsequent urges.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about personality disorders, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this country that is home to a canal that connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
This treaty, which was signed in 1903 by the US Secretary of State and an envoy to Panama, gave the United States control of the Panama Canal in exchange for ten million dollars.
This dictator and drug trafficker, who was nicknamed "Pineapple Face," ruled Panama from 1983 until 1989, when he was captured by the United States during Operation Just Cause.

bonuses.leadin: During the 1970s, Omar Torrijos [torr-EE-hos] was dictator of this country, which had earlier gained independence in 1903 from Colombia. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with duodenum, jejunum, ileum.
What is the main function of the duodenum in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to duodenum, jejunum, ileum.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name these reactions in which a group is removed from a molecule.

Zaitsev's rule predicts that the stable, more substituted one of these compounds will be produced in elimination reactions. They can be produced via the hydrogenation of alkynes using Lindlar's catalyst.
This scientist names an elimination reaction that violates Zaitsev's rule and begins with a step of exhaustive methylation. His namesake rearrangement converts an amide into an amine.

bonuses.leadin: These reactions are subject to Zaitsev's rule and have either E1 or E2 mechanisms. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these mathematical arguments that demonstrate the truth of a statement. In geometry they are often done in two-column form.
This type of proof is often used to prove the square root of 2 is irrational. It operates by assuming a statement is true and showing it leads to an impossible result.
Proofs by Contradiction rely on this law of logic, which states that a statement or its negation must be true.

bonuses.leadin: When these arguments are made with n=k and then n=k+1, they are inductive. For 10 points each--

parts.text: Heracles was sent to the swamps of Lerna to kill this poison-breathing serpent which had many heads, only one of which was immortal.
The Hydra was aided in the fight when one of these creatures belonging to Hera emerged from its cave and bit Heracles' foot. It was later turned into a constellation.
This son of Iphicles helped Heracles by using a torch to cauterize the Hydra's bleeding necks and thereby slowing its regrowth.

bonuses.leadin: Identify some things about the second labor of Heracles for 10 points each.

parts.text: Identify this politician, the first Black congresswoman. This politician was also the first Black person to run for the presidential nomination of a major political party.
Chisholm hoped to defeat this incumbent president in 1972. This president resigned two years later in the wake of the Watergate scandal.

After this politician was shot, Chisholm controversially visited him in the hospital, leading to an unlikely political alliance in which this politician helped Chisholm pass a minimum wage law for domestic workers. This violently racist governor of Alabama opposed the integration of the University of Alabama with his Stand in the Schoolhouse Door.

bonuses.leadin: This politician's campaign slogan for the 1972 presidential election was "unbought and unbossed," which later became the title of her autobiography. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This webcomic by David Morgan-Mar features lego figures. One story arc features the author becoming a Death and killing himself. Despite its name, it updates extremely regularly, and recently passed the 3000 strip mark.

This webcomic's title comes from a strip in which a character buys cotton candy made of the two title substances. Published daily by Kris, Rob, Matt, and Dave, it is known for its characteristically dark humor.

This webcomic used to be about indie music, but now it's about the life of Marten Reed and his friends. Characters include Hannelore and Faye, who work at the Coffee of Doom shop, as well as the Yelling Bird, who is not a Native American.

parts.text: One of the state's largest Hmong communities is located in this capital city of California.
Fresno, which has over 24,000 Hmong residents, is the largest city in this California valley, whose other cities include Bakersfield and Stockton.
This city in the San Joaquin (san wah-KEEN) Valley, nicknamed the "Gateway to Yosemite," is around 20% Hmong, as recounted in The Spirit Catches You and You Fall Down.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about parts of California with large populations of Hmong (mung) people.

parts.text: Name this type of learning. Its classical type is exemplified by Pavlov's dogs, which salivated upon hearing a bell due to their association between its ringing and food.
In this demonstration of conditioning, a baby was introduced to white rats and began to associate them with impending loud noise, developing a fear of furry objects.
This Hopkins psychologist and founder of the Behaviorist school performed the Kerplunk experiment on rats in mazes in addition to studying Little Albert with Rosalie Rayner.

bonuses.leadin: Its "operant" type involves reinforcement or punishment. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with alveoli structure and function.
What is the main function of the bronchus in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to alveoli structure and function.

parts.text: Name this twenty seventh ruler of the Holy Roman Empire who ruled from 1355 to 1378 from his home in Prague.

Before becoming Holy Roman Emperor, Charles ruled this kingdom in what is now the Czech Republic. The name of this kingdom has become synonymous with an artistic lifestyle that is outside of conventional societal norms.
Charles IV built this defensive wall in order to strengthen the fortifications of Prague Castle. According to myth, the purpose of this wall was not strategic but to employ and thus feed the poor.

parts.text: In this general process, the basic mechanism of evolution, organisms with harmful mutations die before becoming parents, while those with beneficial mutations live longer and have more offspring.

The chief British proponent of natural selection was this man who popularized the theory by coining the phrase "survival of the fittest" to summarize it. His two major works are Social Statics and A System of Synthetic Philosophy.
In this process, suggested as a biological basis for altruism, the fitness and genetic similarity of relatives comes into account when determining mates.
